subject: Request: tighter RTO for multi-region failover — Aurabank
messages:
From: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@aurabank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: tighter RTO for multi-region failover (Aurabank)

Hi Aditya / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare our internal risk acceptance memo, security and ops have pushed back on the RTO/RPO numbers in the standard contract for multi-region failover. Specifically: we need an RTO <= 1 hour for the primary transaction ingestion path and an RPO <= 10 minutes for the tokenization pipeline during regional failover.

We understand this is tighter than your published regional SLA. For our regulatory audit we need a documented exception (or an interim operational commitment) that covers:
- Scope: what endpoints/routes are covered (we only need the ingestion path and tokenization service)
- Measurables: how RTO/RPO will be measured and reported
- Bridge/startup obligations: any runbook or warm-standby requirements on both sides
- Remedies: if SLA is missed, what credits or mitigations apply

Attached is a short note from our compliance team summarizing audit expectations (Aurabank_SLA_Request.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can support an exception or an interim plan while we finalize procurement?

Priya Reddy
Head of Cloud Risk, Aurabank
priya.reddy@aurabank.com
Attachments: Aurabank_SLA_Request.pdf

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Jul 2028 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tighter RTO for multi-region failover (Aurabank)

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Priya's ask; copied their compliance note. High-level thoughts:

- The ask (1h RTO / 10m RPO for two critical routes) is more aggressive than our standard multi-region warm-standby posture. We typically offer 2-3h RTO windows in the hosted product for full failovers unless the customer is on Dedicated with reserved standby capacity.

- Potential path to approval (operational + contractual):
  1) Interim operational commitment: Offer a conditional 2-hour RTO + 15-minute RPO for the two routes, with defined pre-warm/activation checklist and prioritized capacity during the term.
  2) Capacity-backed carveout: If customer commits to Dedicated capacity (or a reserved warm-standby add-on) we can tighten to 1-hour RTO / 10-minute RPO for those routes. This requires a short capacity sizing exercise and a one-off prep window.
  3) Measurement & reporting: instrument route-level synthetic checks (we can provide dashboard links) and weekly RTO/RPO reports during the first 90 days post-go-live.
  4) Remedies: limited SLA credits tied to route-level availability (caps to avoid outsized financial exposure). Legal will need to draft a short addendum.

Action items: Marissa, can you engage Solutions/Legal on a draft interim addendum (suggest the attached redwood-interim-sla-draft.docx as starting point)? Karthik, can infra run a quick capacity estimate for a reserved warm-standby for ingestion+tokenization?

I'll prepare a reply to Priya by EOD tomorrow with an operational proposal + timeline.

Thanks,
Aditya
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@aurabank.com>, procurement@aurabank.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tighter RTO for multi-region failover (Aurabank)

Priya — thanks for the clear ask and the compliance note. We appreciate the constraints you're under. Below is a concrete, time-bound proposal we can put into an addendum for procurement to review.

Summary proposal (interim commitment):
- Scope: warm-standby coverage limited to the ingestion API (POST /v1/ingest) and the tokenization async pipeline (tokenizer-v2) across two primary regions (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 secondary).
- Operational commitment: 2-hour RTO; 15-minute RPO for covered routes during a regional failover event.
- Path to 1-hour RTO / 10-minute RPO: requires a Dedicated reserved warm-standby pool (one-time sizing + pre-warm window). If Aurabank signs up for the reserved warm-standby add-on within 60 days of go-live, Redwood will commit to 1-hour RTO / 10-minute RPO for the scoped routes from the activation date of that add-on.
- Measurement: Redwood will publish route-level synthetic monitors and an incident timeline for any activation; RTO will be measured from failover trigger to confirmed route acceptance in the secondary region; RPO will be measured based on replication lag observed by our persistence layer and tokenization queue offsets. We will provide weekly RTO/RPO reports for the first 90 days post-go-live.
- Remedies & caps: SLA credits up to 10% of monthly usage for missed SLA on scoped routes; credits are limited to incidents where Redwood is the primary cause (not third-party links).
- Preconditions: Aurabank executes the addendum and approves a pre-warm test window (2 business days) prior to go-live. Redwood requires runbook sign-off and a joint DR exercise within first 30 days.

Attachments: redwood-interim-sla-draft.docx (draft addendum with definitions, measurement language, and credit table).

Next steps:
1) If this aligns, we'll send the addendum to procurement and Legal (DocuSign-ready).
2) Karthik's team will send a sizing worksheet for the reserved warm-standby option (if you want to accelerate to 1-hour RTO).
3) Schedule a joint runbook review + DR dry-run (45–60 minute session) before go-live.

Links: HubSpot ticket: https://hubspot.com/contacts/AUR-2028-0421 — I've attached the draft to the ticket.

If you prefer we can also schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the technical acceptance criteria.

Best,
Aditya Rao
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-interim-sla-draft.docx

Date: Sat, 7 Jul 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tighter RTO for multi-region failover (Aurabank)

Aditya / team — thanks, this is helpful and addresses most of our auditors' concerns. Two quick follow-ups before we sign the addendum:

1) Can you include a short paragraph in the addendum stating Redwood's access controls during the DR exercise and whether any customer data will be exposed to on-call engineers during activation? Auditors want explicit language.
2) We will start sizing in parallel — procurement and infra will review the reserved warm-standby worksheet. If the capacity numbers look off we may request a short calibration run.

Assuming the access-control paragraph is included, procurement is comfortable moving forward with the interim 2-hour/15-minute commitment and the 60-day path to 1-hour/10-minute once reserved capacity is in place. Please send the DocuSign-ready addendum and we'll aim to turn it in this week.

Thanks,
Priya
Attachments: none
